title: Label the Crates
story:
Taped to crate 0417, in Tomasz's capital letters:

THE INVENTORY SYSTEM READS METADATA FROM THE IMAGE, NOT FROM ANYONE'S MEMORY. EVERY CRATE IMAGE NEEDS A STATION LABEL, ITS OWN CRATE ID, AND A KNOWN WORKING DIRECTORY. THE CRATE ID MUST NOT BE TYPED INTO THE FILE; IT IS PASSED IN AT BUILD TIME, OR WE WILL FORGET TO CHANGE IT.

Build `kestrel/crate:2.0` from `alpine:3.20` with a label `station=kestrel-point`, a label and an environment variable both carrying the crate ID `C-0417` (supplied as a build argument), and the working directory `/crate`.
objectives: Label `station=kestrel-point` and label `crate-id` equal to the build argument value
Environment variable `CRATE_ID` equal to the same value, and `WORKDIR /crate`
hints: Image metadata is set by Dockerfile instructions that describe the image rather than doing work. A build-time variable is declared with one instruction and fed a value from the command line.

Declare `ARG CRATE_ID`, then reuse it as `$CRATE_ID` in `ENV` and `LABEL`. Use `WORKDIR` for the directory, and pass the value with `docker build --build-arg NAME=value`. Give the ARG a default like `UNASSIGNED` so a forgotten flag is obvious.

```bash
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
ARG CRATE_ID=UNASSIGNED
LABEL station="kestrel-point" crate-id="$CRATE_ID"
ENV CRATE_ID=$CRATE_ID
WORKDIR /crate
EOF
docker build --build-arg CRATE_ID=C-0417 -t kestrel/crate:2.0 .
```

validation.description: Environment variable `CRATE_ID=C-0417` is set in the image

solution:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
ARG CRATE_ID=UNASSIGNED
LABEL station="kestrel-point" crate-id="$CRATE_ID"
ENV CRATE_ID=$CRATE_ID
WORKDIR /crate
EOF
debrief: `ARG` exists only while building, while `ENV` persists into containers and `LABEL` records metadata that tools can query. Pro tip: read labels back with `docker image inspect -f '{{json .Config.Labels}}' IMAGE | jq`.
